text:
maya: onboarding Orchid/cobalt-13b today. doing int8 dynamic pipeline, but early evals show single-token collapse in long completions :confused:

ravi: single-token collapse as in repeating tokens?

maya: yes, after ~600 tokens it tends to repeat a stopword pattern til timeout. fp16 baseline doesn't.

sylvia: repeating often comes from rotary mismatch or pos-emb off-by-one when kv cache state is streamed. any vocab oddities?

maya: vendor used a split-case tokenizer: duplicates lowercase + uppercase entries for same surface form. they also reserve id 65535 as a "marker" for ligature boundaries.

alex: 65535 is out-of-range for some converters if we assume 16-bit safe maps. that could cause wrap-around when casting to int32 in tokenmap. check for modulo collisions.

maya: good call. my conversion initially coerced to np.uint16 and then to int, which wrapped 65535 -> -1 in one helper. oops. fixed that to explicit mapping to 1M offset and then remap to gap area.

triage-bot: conversion job 49101 submitted. artifacts: s3://redwood-onboard/cobalt/49101/

ravi: kube-ctl logs from quant worker show many outlier activations in attn_proj layer during calibration. were you using symmetric per-tensor int8?

maya: yes default symmetric per-tensor. quant hist shows heavy tail for ~5% of channels. tried per-channel for proj, negligible perf hit for int8 runtime.

sylvia: if proj per-channel helps, try freezing query/key/out_proj to int16->int8 hybrid? we did that before for orion7b.

maya: tried three variants: dyn-int8 (A), per-channel-proj dyn-int8 (B), hybrid-outproj int16 + dyn-int8 (C). small-run results: A ppl=21.7, B ppl=20.1, C ppl=19.5 vs fp16 19.3. embeddings avg-cos: A drop 0.15, B drop 0.06, C drop 0.02.

alex: C looks promising. but why collapse after long contexts? maybe kv position meta from vendor starts at 0 but they included an extraneous BOS token in stream. index mismatch accumulates when streaming partials.

maya: dug into stream metadata. vendor's stream header: {"seq_start":1, "baked_bos":true} 1 refers to human 1-based seq. our stream parser assumes seq_start=0 and strips BOS ourselves. double-BOS leads to offset in positional embeddings in cache.

sylvia: that would misalign rotary phases when reusing cached kvs. add a guard: if baked_bos true, don't strip and decrement seq_start when merging caches. also add a test for duplicate BOS id in tokenmap.

ravi: we should also assert no id collisions after tokenmap remap. earlier you remapped 65535 into a gap; confirm that gap doesn't contain sentinel or BOS.

maya: the gap we used was 50200-50299, empty in vendor vocab. confirmed no collision. added dedupe check to converter.

triage-bot: eval jobs queued: 49102 (A), 49103 (B), 49104 (C). ETA ~4h.

triage-bot: eval 49102 done: ppl=21.7, embed_drop=0.15, repeats=high.

triage-bot: eval 49103 done: ppl=20.1, embed_drop=0.06, repeats=medium.

triage-bot: eval 49104 done: ppl=19.5, embed_drop=0.02, repeats=low.

maya: C still not perfect on very long noisy prompts, but much better. keep out_proj int16 as default opt for cobalt-13b int8 profile.

sylvia: add a note in models/cobalt/notes.md explaining: 1) vendor baked_bos stream flag, 2) high-id sentinel 65535 remapped, 3) proj-per-channel helpful, 4) whitelist out_proj int16 for int8 profiles.

alex: i'll open a small converter PR with tests: one for 65535 handling, one for baked_bos merge semantics, one for dedupe tokenmap.

ravi: once PR lands, schedule a smoke on staging dedicated cluster (int8 runtime) to check latency regressions from per-channel scaling and int16 out_proj. we need to measure tokens/sec and p95 latency.

maya: will run longer QA generator set overnight (~1000 anchors) and post CSV in morning. thanks folks. :rocket:
